newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African rand gold price at eleven-month low.
newsitem.headline: S.African rand gold price at eleven-month low.

text.p: The rand gold price fell to its lowest level in eleven months on Friday as the dollar gold price slumped to an almost four year low and the rand continued its rally against the U.S. unit.

In late afternoon trade, gold was quoted at 1,508 rand an ounce -- its lowest level since February 7 last year -- as the dollar gold price fell below the $340 mark and the rand strengthened to its best level since July last year.
The result on the local stock market was a 34.5 point drop in the all gold index to 1355.4, just 16 points shy of a 13-month low.
Analysts said the falling price held dire prospects for South African gold mines in the first quarter of this year.
"I think in general a lot of operations are going to be very marginalised in the current quarter," said Dean Cunningham, gold analyst at stockbrokers Fergusson Bros.

Edward Osborn, strategic economist at Edey Rogers and Co said in a recent article written for Reuters that working profits at South African gold mines could plummet by over a billion rand in the current quarter.

"On the assumptions of an average grade of five grams per tonne, an inflation of working costs per tonne from quarter-to-quarter of five percent, and an average working revenue falling back to 1,615 rand per ounce, working profit will collapse in the first quarter of 1997 to a mere 270 million rand -- as compared with the 1,520 million rand in the fourth quarter of 1996," Osborn said.
"We need to see an improvement in the rand gold price," Cunningham said.
While few market players are prepared to call a top to the rand's current rally, Cunnigham said he was optimistic that the gold price would find a bottom by the second quarter.

He said there were signs that interest in the metals markets was beginning to develop as the global economic outlook improved. "I also know for a fact that the fundamental fabrication demand is there," he said.

"When you look at global markets..bonds strong, equities strong, at some stage they are going to look unattractive on a medium-term view and hopefully some of that demand for equities will sway towards precious metals and possibly gold," Cunningham said.
Cunningham felt, however, that a gold price of over $360 in the short-term was premature.
"But I think below 340 it has to be a steal given the basic fundamental demand outlooks," he added.
